image_query: Shore Temple Mahabalipuram Bay of Bengal photograph
tweets: The Shore Temple, Māmallapuram — raised by Pallava king Narasiṃhavarman II around 700 CE. Its neighbours here were carved from single boulders; this one was built stone by dressed stone, three shrines set to greet the Bay of Bengal at sunrise for over 1300 years.

European sailors named this coast the 'Seven Pagodas', believing sunken temples lay offshore. In 2004, the tsunami's retreat briefly exposed carved stone remains in the shallows — old legend, sudden echo. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
